study: TEA & environmental assessment of SAF from forest residues (FT-SPK)
their_var: Cost of forest residues (feedstock supply cost at refinery)
their_baseline: $12.6 million total (97% of material cost); MSP baseline $2.50/kg at 10% IRR
range_justification: Stated observed spread of feedstock price ('varies widely'), no cited source for the range; drives SAF production cost $1.41-2.27/kg
quote: The cost of forest residues varies widely, ranging from $20 to $80 per tonne. This can cause the SAF production cost to increase from $1.41 per kg to $2.27 per kg.

study: TEA & environmental assessment of SAF from forest residues (FT-SPK)
range_justification: Illustrative example of cost-estimate uncertainty; no cited source
quote: if inflation increases up to 4%, it can increase the unit production cost to $1.93 per kg.

study: TEA & environmental assessment of SAF from forest residues (FT-SPK)
their_var: Steam usage (steam consumption, kg per kg SAF) — usage amount, not an emission factor
range_justification: Assumed +/-20% perturbation on process steam demand; GW impact spans 6 to 42.7 gCO2eq/kg. No cited source
quote: When steam usage is increased by 20% to 0.42 kg kg-1, the GW impact increases to 42.7 gCO2 eq. per kg... a 20% reduction in steam usage decreases the GW impact to 6 gCO2 eq. per kg.

study: TEA & environmental assessment of SAF from forest residues (FT-SPK)
their_var: Electricity usage (kW h per kg SAF) — usage amount, not grid CI
their_baseline: ~0.128 kW h kg-1 (implied; +20% = 0.154 kW h kg-1)
range_justification: Assumed +/-20% perturbation on electricity demand; GWP spans 6.89 to 41.9 gCO2eq/kg. No cited source
quote: increasing electricity usage by 20% to 0.154 kW h kg results in a GWP impact of 41.9 gCO2 eq. per kg, while a 20% decrease reduces it to 6.89 gCO2 eq. per kg.

study: TEA & environmental assessment of SAF from forest residues (FT-SPK)
range_justification: Assumed reduction to 80% to test sensitivity; GWP rises to 32.7 gCO2eq/kg. No cited source
quote: a decrease in Fischer-Tropsch conversion efficiency to 80% from 100% shows an increase in GWP to 32.7 gCO2 eq. per kg of SAF.

study: TEA & environmental assessment of SAF from forest residues (FT-SPK)
their_var: Forest residue requirement (feedstock quantity, not price)
range_justification: Assumed +/-20% perturbation; GWP 23.8 to 25.3 gCO2eq/kg. No cited source
quote: Variations in forest residue requirements by +/-20% lead to GWP values ranging from 23.8 to 25.3 gCO2 eq. per kg of SAF.

study: TEA & environmental assessment of SAF from forest residues (FT-SPK)
range_justification: Perturbation tested; minor impact, GWI 24.4 to 24.8 gCO2eq/kg. No cited source or explicit range
quote: changes in diethanolamine requirements for gas treatment show a minor impact on GWI, varying from 24.4 to 24.8 gCO2 eq. per kg of SAF.
